messages:
john.c (customer): Hey team — after we switched to the PrivateLink endpoint for Redwood API, we've been seeing intermittent 503s and TLS handshake failures from our app. Started ~0900 UTC.

maya (support): sorry to hear that, digging in. can you share a `curl -v` from one of the app hosts and the pod/node?

john.c (customer): pasted quick output: `curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:10.12.45.78` -> TLS handshake fail: `verify error:num=62:hostname mismatch` then sometimes `HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable`.

alex (sre): couple quick questions: 1) is your app doing SNI? 2) are you resolving the service to the interface ENI IP or to the public NLB IP by mistake? 3) any NAT gateway/proxy in the path?

john.c (customer): app uses default http client so SNI should be set by hostname. Our resolver returns 10.12.45.78 (interface endpoint IP). We do have a NAT GW for other traffic but thought traffic to PrivateLink stays local.

sam (eng-infra): can you run `openssl s_client -connect 10.12.45.78:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts` and paste the cert subject/SANs? also `dig +short api.redwood.example.com` from the same host.

john.c (customer): `dig` -> `10.12.45.78`. openssl shows leaf cert CN=api.redwood.io, SANs=[api.redwood.io, *.redwood.io]. Our hostname is `api.redwood.example.com` (customer's domain via CNAME to Redwood). Might explain mismatch?

maya (support): aha — looks like the TLS cert presented is for Redwood's domain, but you fronted it with your custom domain. Did you configure TLS via the Redwood console for your custom domain and upload cert / enable ALIAS?

john.c (customer): we set up a CNAME from `api.redwood.example.com` -> `api.redwood-inference.redwood.internal` as instructed and toggled custom domain in console (status says provisioning). We assumed PrivateLink would hit the same cert bundle.

alex (sre): two possible causes: 1) DNS split-horizon: your VPC resolver is returning the PrivateLink ENI IP but the private hosted zone record used by the custom domain isn't yet associated with the VPC — so requests sometimes route to fallback public NLB that has Redwood cert for `*.redwood.io`. 2) egress/proxy rewriting Host/SNI or a outbound proxy is redirecting to public endpoint.

sam (eng-infra): also check the interface endpoint security group inbound rules: the ENI will only accept traffic from allowed CIDRs. If some subnets go through a NATGW/proxy the source IP will be NATed and may be blocked by the endpoint SG -> intermittent. Run `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=private-ip-address,Values=10.12.45.78` to find ENI id and SGs.

john.c (customer): ran the ENI lookup: eni-0a1b2c3d, SGs: sg-aaa111 (allow 10.12.0.0/16:443). Our app nodes are in 10.12.45.0/24 so should match.

maya (support): can you `tcpdump -n -i eth0 port 443` on the app host while reproducing and confirm dst IP is 10.12.45.78 and there are no outgoing packets to public IPs? Also check `traceroute -n 10.12.45.78` to ensure path stays inside VPC.

john.c (customer): tcpdump shows initial SYN->10.12.45.78 then we sometimes see subsequent flows to 3.120.45.90 (public) — looks like occasional fallback. Why would that happen?

alex (sre): likely DNS TTL or client resolver logic: if a PrivateLink ENI is unhealthy in one AZ, the service provider's DNS can return a public fallback IP (or the client resolver may try alternate records). Also check route tables: if the app's subnet route table has an explicit route to NAT for 10.12.0.0/16 (misconfigured) it could SNAT. Any custom route propagation with TGW?

sam (eng-infra): confirm the VPC DHCP option set uses AmazonProvidedDNS (so you get the VPC resolver behavior). If you are using an external DNS forwarder it might incorrectly cache public IPs. Also check that the Private Hosted Zone for `api.redwood.example.com` is associated with the VPC — if not, Route53 could return the public record.

john.c (customer): DHCP is AmazonProvidedDNS. Our Route53 private hosted zone for `redwood.internal` is associated. But our custom domain is under `redwood.example.com` — we created a CNAME to `api.redwood-inference.ap-southeast-1.vpce.amazonaws.com`. Maybe the private hosted zone for the vpce name isn't present.

maya (support): two actions: 1) confirm private hosted zone for provider-owned endpoint names is associated to your VPC (or we recommend you point the CNAME to the service-specific private DNS name we provided). 2) while provisioning the custom domain we need the TLS mapping to complete on the Redwood side — verify in console the custom domain status is `ready` not `provisioning`. If cert provisioning falls back to the public NLB you'll see our cert.

sam (eng-infra): also check NACLs and endpoint SG egress rules. If the ENI cannot reach Redwood's CA validation or ACME servers because of egress allowlist, cert provisioning can fail and you may get the default cert. If your environment has strict egress allowlists, allow outbound to these Redwood ACME IP ranges or `acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org` etc.

john.c (customer): we do have an egress allowlist — only a handful of external IPs allowed. That could explain provisioning failure. How do we check cert provisioning logs?

maya (support): I can check on our side — can you confirm the account org id and give me the custom domain name? I will look for provisioning errors. Meanwhile please add temporary egress to ACME endpoints for the provisioning window and re-run verification.

john.c (customer): domain `api.redwood.example.com`, account 987654321. adding allowlist rule now for `159.89.22.11` (ACME) and `52.24.1.12` (our internal test host).

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-11-02T09:12:30Z: custom-domain-provisioning started for account 987654321, domain api.redwood.example.com

maya (support): I see a provisioning failure on our side earlier: `timeout talking to ACME servers`. I've retriggered provisioning now that you've opened egress. Please confirm after ~5-10m.

john.c (customer): retesting now — `curl -v` shows `subjectAltName: DNS:api.redwood.example.com` and no more hostname mismatch. Requests over PrivateLink are consistent and no public IP fallbacks seen in tcpdump. latency looks good. Thanks! :tada:

maya (support): great — root causes: (1) egress allowlist blocked cert provisioning so client saw default provider cert, (2) intermittent DNS/resolve fallback to public IP when provisioning/unhealthy endpoints. Action items: document require egress to ACME + ensure private host zone association + verify endpoint SG/route tables. I'll follow up with a checklist for onboarding PrivateLink customers.

alex (sre): adding note: if you rely on custom domains with PrivateLink, it's best to stage a temporary egress window for cert provisioning and to validate Route53 private zone associations per AZ to avoid split-horizon.

john.c (customer): will do. thanks all for quick help! :heart:
